patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient has been experiencing progressive left leg pain for 2 months, with recent interference with sleep. The pain was initially treated as 'growing pains' with ibuprofen, without improvement. He recalls being hit in the thigh by a baseball one week before the onset of symptoms, resulting in redness and swelling that lasted several days.

Secondary_Symptoms: History of trauma to the leg

patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: No fever, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms reported.

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate and diagnose the patient presenting with progressive left leg pain and assess the pathological causes.

turns.doctor_opening: Hello, what brings you in today? Could you tell me about yourself and what's been going on?
turns.patient_opening: “My left leg has been getting progressively more painful for about two months, and it’s started to keep me up at night. It didn’t get better with ibuprofen, and about a week before it started I got hit on the thigh by a baseball, which left redness and swelling for several days.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you have any small, raised bumps on your skin that have a tiny indentation or a "dimple" in the center?
turns.patient_answer: “Not that I’ve noticed—no small raised bumps with a center dimple on my leg.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed that you need to urinate more often than usual?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed needing to urinate more often than usual, and there haven’t been any changes like that.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been feeling generally weak or lacking your usual strength lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t felt weak or noticed any change in my usual strength. I can still walk, but the pain in my left leg is getting worse over time, especially at night.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any difficulty with dressing yourself lately?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any trouble dressing myself or using my arms and hands.” “I mainly just feel the pain in my left leg, and it’s been getting worse over time, especially at night.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any rashes, bumps, or sores appearing specifically along the veins in your arms?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any rashes, bumps, or sores along the veins in my arms. It’s just been the pain in my left leg that’s been getting worse, especially at night.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you been experiencing any itchiness on your skin?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t had any itchiness or skin irritation—just the progressive pain in my left leg. I also haven’t noticed any new rashes or sores.”

turns.doctor_question: Do you experience any pain or cramping in your calves when you walk that feels better once you stop and rest?
turns.patient_answer: “No, when I walk I don’t get calf cramping that improves when I stop and rest—I mainly have a steadily worsening pain in my left leg that’s been bothering me most, especially at night. I can still walk, but it doesn’t really ease up with stopping.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed if your stools have become unusually pale, light-colored, or clay-colored recently?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any change in my stool color—no pale or clay-colored stools. I haven’t had any other symptoms besides the progressively worse left leg pain, especially at night.”

turns.doctor_question: Have you noticed any weakness in your hands, or have you had more difficulty than usual gripping or holding onto objects?
turns.patient_answer: “No, I haven’t noticed any weakness in my hands or any trouble gripping or holding onto objects.”
